mods.title: Introduction to C++
mods.excerpt: Discover how Bjarne Stroustrup added Object-Oriented features to C. Learn about compilation, the standard namespace, and fundamental I/O streams.
mods.body:
C++ was developed by Bjarne Stroustrup at Bell Labs in 1979 as an extension of the C programming language, initially named "C with Classes".

C vs C++

While C is a procedural language, C++ is a multi-paradigm language. It supports procedural, object-oriented, and generic programming. Crucially, almost all valid C code is valid C++ code.

C++ gives you the low-level memory control of C, while providing high-level abstractions like classes and templates.

The Compilation Process

  • Preprocessing — handles #include and #define macros.
  • Compilation — translates code into assembly.
  • Assembly — converts to machine-level object files (.o or .obj).
  • Linking — merges object files and libraries into an executable (.exe).

Standard I/O and Namespaces

C++ uses streams for input and output, defined in the <iostream> library.

#include <iostream>

int main() {
    // using namespace std; is common but often avoided in large projects
    std::cout << "Hello, IT Study Hub!" << std::endl;
    
    int age;
    std::cout << "Enter your age: ";
    std::cin >> age;
    
    return 0;
}

Save as main.cpp → compile with g++ main.cpp -o app → run with ./app.

mods.title: Control Statements
mods.excerpt: The if, switch, while, for and do-while statements are the decision-making backbone of every C++ program. Master these to control execution flow.
mods.body:
Control statements divide into three categories: Selection (choose a path), Iteration (repeat steps), and Jump (exit or skip). They are the building blocks of all program logic.

Selection: if and switch

int marks = 75;
if (marks >= 90) {
    std::cout << "Grade: A";
} else if (marks >= 70) {
    std::cout << "Grade: B";  // This runs
} else {
    std::cout << "Grade: C";
}

Use switch when matching one variable against many specific values:

int day = 3;
switch (day) {
    case 1: std::cout << "Monday"; break;
    case 3: std::cout << "Wednesday"; break; // Runs
    default: std::cout << "Other day";
}
Always use break in switch cases. Without it, execution "falls through" to the next case!

Iteration: Loops

// while — checks condition first
int i = 0;
while (i < 5) { std::cout << i; i++; }

// do-while — runs at least ONCE
do { std::cout << "Runs once!"; } while (false);

// for — best when iteration count is known
for (int j = 0; j < 5; j++) { std::cout << j; }

mods.title: Classes & Objects
mods.excerpt: Transition from procedural C to object-oriented C++. Learn to define classes, instantiate objects, and use constructors and access specifiers properly.
mods.body:
A class is a blueprint — it defines what data (attributes) and behaviors (methods) objects will have. An object is an instance of that blueprint.

Defining a Class

Unlike structs in C, classes in C++ have members that are private by default. Always remember the semicolon at the end of a class definition!

#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Student {
private:
    int age;

public:
    string name;
    
    // Method declaration
    void display();
    
    // Setter
    void setAge(int a) {
        if (a > 0) age = a;
    }
};

// Method definition outside class using Scope Resolution ::
void Student::display() {
    cout << "Name: " << name << ", Age: " << age << endl;
}

Constructors and Destructors

A constructor runs when an object is created. A destructor (starts with ~) runs when the object goes out of scope.

class Player {
public:
    Player() { cout << "Player Spawned!" << endl; }
    ~Player() { cout << "Player Destroyed!" << endl; }
};

int main() {
    Player p1; // Prints "Spawned"
    return 0;  // Prints "Destroyed" as p1 goes out of scope
}

mods.title: Pointers & Memory Management
mods.excerpt: C++ gives you direct access to memory. Master pointers, references, and dynamic memory allocation using new and delete to prevent memory leaks.
mods.body:
A pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable. They are powerful but require careful management.

Basics of Pointers and References

int score = 100;
int* ptr = &score;  // ptr holds the memory address of score

cout << score;      // Prints 100
cout << ptr;        // Prints memory address (e.g., 0x7ffe...)
cout << *ptr;       // Prints 100 (Dereferencing)

// Reference (Alias)
int& ref = score;
ref = 200;          // score is now 200

Dynamic Memory Allocation

Unlike stack memory, which is managed automatically, heap memory must be managed manually using new and delete.

int* dPtr = new int; // Allocate memory on the heap
*dPtr = 50;

cout << *dPtr << endl;

delete dPtr;         // Free the memory!
dPtr = nullptr;      // Prevent dangling pointer
Rule of thumb: For every new, there must be a matching delete. Failing to do this causes a memory leak.

Allocating Arrays

int* arr = new int[10]; // Array of 10 integers
arr[0] = 5;
delete[] arr;           // Use delete[] for arrays!

mods.title: Inheritance & Polymorphism
mods.excerpt: Inheritance builds relationships between classes. Virtual functions and polymorphism allow one interface to take many forms, enabling dynamic dispatch.
mods.body:
Inheritance promotes code reusability. C++ allows single, multiple, and hierarchical inheritance.

Basic Inheritance

class Animal {
public:
    void eat() { cout << "Eating..." << endl; }
};

class Dog : public Animal {
public:
    void bark() { cout << "Woof!" << endl; }
};

Dog d;
d.eat();  // Inherited from Animal
d.bark();

Runtime Polymorphism & Virtual Functions

To achieve dynamic method resolution at runtime, use the virtual keyword in the base class and override it in the derived class.

class Animal {
public:
    virtual void sound() { cout << "..." << endl; }
};

class Cat : public Animal {
public:
    void sound() override { cout << "Meow!" << endl; }
};

Animal* ptr = new Cat();
ptr->sound(); // Outputs "Meow!" because of the virtual keyword
delete ptr;

Abstract Classes

A class with at least one pure virtual function (= 0) is abstract and cannot be instantiated. It acts like an interface.

class Shape {
public:
    virtual double area() = 0; // Pure virtual function
};

mods.title: Exception Handling
mods.excerpt: C++ provides mechanisms to handle runtime errors gracefully. Learn how to throw exceptions, catch them, and use the standard exception library.
mods.body:
Exception handling in C++ separates error-handling code from normal program logic using try, catch, and throw.

The try-catch Block

#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    int denominator = 0;
    
    try {
        if (denominator == 0) {
            throw "Division by zero error!"; // Throws a string literal
        }
        int result = 10 / denominator;
    } 
    catch (const char* msg) {
        cout << "Error: " << msg << endl;
    }
    
    return 0;
}

Standard Exceptions

It's best practice to use classes from the <stdexcept> library instead of throwing primitive types.

#include <stdexcept>

void validateAge(int age) {
    if (age < 0) {
        throw std::invalid_argument("Age cannot be negative");
    }
}

// In main:
try {
    validateAge(-5);
} catch (const std::invalid_argument& e) {
    cout << e.what() << endl; // Always catch by const reference!
}

mods.title: Templates & Generic Programming
mods.excerpt: Write code once that works for any data type. Templates are the foundation of generic programming and the driving force behind the Standard Template Library.

mods.title: Standard Template Library (STL)
mods.excerpt: Do not reinvent the wheel. The STL provides highly optimized containers, algorithms, and iterators. Vectors and Maps will become your best friends.

mods.title: Modern C++ & Smart Pointers
mods.excerpt: Forget manual memory management. C++11 introduced Smart Pointers that automatically clean up memory, drastically reducing memory leaks and segfaults.

mods.title: File Handling & Streams
mods.excerpt: Persist your data. Learn how to read from and write to text and binary files using fstream, ifstream, and ofstream.

mods.title: Multithreading (C++11)
mods.excerpt: Harness the full power of modern multi-core processors. Learn to spawn threads, synchronize them with mutexes, and avoid race conditions.

mods.title: RAII & Rule of Three
mods.excerpt: Write professional, leak-proof C++. Understand RAII principles and know exactly when you need to define custom copy constructors and assignment operators.
